situation: After a night in which my vigilante shot gave concrete feedback (a revealed kill of an evil player, or an immune result exposing the Serial Killer), only a few players are alive. The remaining evil faction is isolated, and the day needs a decisive lead. Information landscape: Rich in mechanics: GM-announced night deaths, dead town wills, healer save history, and my private shot feedback that can be matched against the public report. Stakes: The board is late-game with few players left. One correct vote or shot can eliminate the last evil faction or the second killer, and a wrong one risks a town loss. Using verified information decides the game. Consensus: The village is receptive and looking for a lead. Wills, save history and announcements are credible, and they rally behind a claim that fits them. My position: Driving the discussion and framing the choice between a vote now and a night shot. Heat: Low to zero. The announced kill or the confirmed mechanic backs my claim, apart from the accused player's attempt to call it a late fabrication. Forward exposure: A hard claim gives up role secrecy and makes me the likely target of the night kill or a block from the remaining evil factions. It cannot be undone. It is worth it because the claim is verifiable and moves the town toward the right target. Target landscape: The remaining pool is small: claimed or unverified town roles, a quiet player, a spent role, and a neutral. One candidate is pinned by my shot result (the immune player), or the evil pool is narrowed by the dead wolves. Evidence comes from mechanics, not behavior. Public vs private: I privately know exactly whom I shot and what came back (a kill that matches the GM announcement, or an immune notice with no public attack). The public only sees the morning report and cannot yet link it to me.

action: At four alive with a wolf still living and you holding a bullet, keep the vigilante role and the bullet hidden. Build your standing on whatever confirmed evidence clears you, such as a dead Town player's will or announced roles. Frame the vote as a choice between the remaining unverified players, and push on their records and votes. If you are already publicly cleared, lead the debate from that standing. If you are not cleared, make your case on records and votes rather than revealing the shot. A claimed vigilante with a known bullet is the obvious night kill and the wolves' priority, so a hidden bullet is the only thing that survives the night.
situation: Four players remain at the parity threshold with one hidden wolf, possibly alongside a lone killer. The vigilante is publicly cleared or unnoticed and holds a bullet that no one knows about. Information landscape: Information-rich. Dead roles and wills are confirmed, a lone killer or other roles may already be gone, and the remaining players' records are partly known. Stakes: At four alive, one wrong vote or one night kill hands the wolves parity. The hidden bullet is a reserve that lets you answer a mislynch, so protecting it from the wolves' kill matters more than showing it off. Consensus: The living players accept the cleared player's lead and turn scrutiny on each other, with no strong rival theory. My position: driving Heat: Low to none. A revealed will or confirmed role clears you and the room treats you as Town. Forward exposure: Claiming vigilante would be irreversible. It would mark you as the wolves' mandatory night kill and give up the hidden-bullet option. Staying quiet costs nothing and can be reversed later. Target landscape: Two or three unverified living players, unclaimed or with contested claims. The choice rests on voting records and behavior, with no hard role confirmation for them. Public vs private: Publicly you are a cleared or ordinary Town player, confirmed by a revealed will. Privately you hold an unfired vigilante bullet the surviving wolf does not know about.

action: Before leading an accusation at four alive, check each mechanical claim against the game rules. Watching, following and checking are all visits, so a Sentinel who says they visited while watching is stating the rule correctly, not lying. Do not treat a rules confusion or a visit-semantics slip as proof of wolfhood. Press for concrete, testable evidence instead, such as who each claimed result named and whether the claims fit the dead players' wills and the morning reports. Cast your vote only on contradictions that survive that check. Hold back a public claim of your remaining bullet until a contradiction is proven.
situation: With four alive and one wolf left, two claimed information roles dispute whether a watch counts as a visit. The vigilante must decide which to push toward elimination. Information landscape: Information-rich on paper, with revealed wills and announced deaths. Two living investigative claims clash, and the dispute turns on rules interpretation. Stakes: A mislynch at four alive lets the wolf reach parity, and with the vigilante's bullet exposed the night kill ends the game. The rules check must come before the vote. Consensus: Votes are splitting between a conflicting claimant and a quiet player, and the room is easily swayed by a loud accusation. My position: driving Heat: Moderate to high. The unclaimed player and a claimant are questioning or accusing you before the vote. Forward exposure: Openly claiming vigilante and driving the vote commits you to the accusation and makes you the wolves' night kill. A wrong lynch cannot be undone and leaves no margin. Target landscape: A binary choice between two conflicting investigative claimants, plus an unclaimed player. The evidence is rules-based and claim-versus-claim rather than confirmed. Public vs private: You privately know you are the true vigilante with a bullet, perhaps one already spent on a miss. Publicly you are claiming and driving a vote on a read that rests on a mechanics misunderstanding.

action: At four alive with one bullet left, treat the day vote and the night shot as a two-step plan. Cast the vote on the suspect backed by the hardest evidence: revealed wills, announced corpse attack types, sigil or check results, or a lie that clearly breaks the stated rules. Keep the bullet for the night. If the vote removes a wolf and the game continues, shoot the remaining suspect that night. If the vote removes the lone killer while a wolf is still alive, expect the wolf to push toward parity, and use the shot or protect your own survival accordingly. If you are unsure between two candidates, do not treat the vote as the only chance, because the surviving bullet can still correct a miss. Do not reveal the bullet publicly unless the claim itself protects you or drives the vote.
situation: Endgame with four players alive, one wolf still alive and possibly a lone killer too. The vigilante holds a last bullet, and the day vote decides whether town stays ahead or hands over parity. Information landscape: Information-rich: dead roles and wills are known and attack types are visible. It is still muddied by conflicting night-action claims and a possible uncountered fake claim. Stakes: Four alive means one wrong elimination plus one night kill leaves the wolf at parity. The vote and the shot together are town's whole margin, so a mis-vote must be recoverable by the bullet. Consensus: The village is nearly deadlocked in a small endgame. Conflicting claims and votes split it, and the vigilante's vote is often the deciding one. My position: driving Heat: Moderate. Opposing players press you to reveal or defend your claim, and the suspected evil players vote against you. Forward exposure: A visible vote is permanent and commits you to that read. Claiming vigilante also marks you as the obvious night kill target for any surviving wolf, and that cannot be undone. The unspent bullet is your only reversible resource. Target landscape: Two or three unverified players, some of them claiming roles such as sentinel, trailseer or sigilist. The split is between a suspect with an evidence-based case and a quiet player acting cautiously. Roles are mostly unconfirmed. Public vs private: You privately hold a live bullet and know your own town status. You usually lack private proof of which remaining player is the wolf or the lone killer, so your read rests on public evidence.

action: When a claimed investigator or sentinel has publicly cleared you or shows consistent, checkable results, and the room is split between a quiet player and an unverified one, vote with the verified claimant against the unverified player whose behavior or past votes fit. Keep your vigilante role hidden and keep your remaining bullet for a night shot at a confirmed suspect. Switch to the majority target only if the verified claimant changes their read or is contradicted by announced facts.
situation: Mid-game with few players left and two evil factions alive. Several town roles are dead, including some with concealed bodies. The day vote splits between a quiet player and an unverified player, and I hold a bullet while the verified investigator leads one side. Information landscape: Information-rich: an investigator check clears me, several roles are revealed, and two bodies were concealed by an illusionist. There are voting records but no confirmed guilty party. Stakes: With six alive and two evil factions, each wrong elimination moves wolves or the killer closer to parity. A split vote that eliminates a lone killer still helps town, but the vote is close enough that each town vote matters. Consensus: The village is split between two suspects. One side follows the dead wolf's earlier pressure on the quiet player. The other follows the investigator's push against the unverified player. Neither side has hard proof. My position: holding out Heat: Low: the claimed investigator cleared me publicly, so suspicion is on other candidates. Forward exposure: My vote is public and permanent, so it commits me to this read. It does not reveal the shooting power and can be revised on later days. If the vote splits from the majority, I risk being marked as an outlier, but heat stays low while a verified claimant has cleared me. Target landscape: A quiet player pushed by a dead wolf's vote, versus an unverified player who voted against a slain tracker. Neither is confirmed. The choice rests on voting records and the verified investigator's lead, not on hard role evidence. Public vs private: The investigator publicly cleared me as not suspicious, and I know I am town holding a live bullet. My private knowledge matches the public read, and I stay concealed while my vote follows the verified information.

action: If you hold unspent bullets and feel the room turning on you, or you are named in the last word, state in your last word that you are the vigilante with bullets left. Point out that your death hands a revealed vigilante body to a possible necromancer, and ask the verified town claimants to vote the unconfirmed suspect instead. Do this before the vote locks rather than staying silent and voting a lone dissenting line. If you are not yet targeted but have no explicit support, align your vote with the verified town bloc rather than a separate unconfirmed target.
situation: After a sigil-confirmed chanteuse death, I voted with the claimed sentinel against an unconfirmed player. The rest of the room, including the verified town core, voted me out 5-2. My two bullets went unspent, and the necromancer then used my body to kill. Information landscape: Information-rich: a dead healer, a dead chanteuse killed by sigil, a concealed casualty, and three verified town claims (investigator, sentinel, sigilist) giving clear visit paths. There was no public evidence against me. Stakes: With seven alive and several evil actors, losing a power role with two bullets unspent is costly. A revealed vigilante body can be used by a necromancer to shoot with no miss penalty, so my elimination arms the enemy as well as costing town its shots. Consensus: A sudden, unprompted bloc formed on me, including the verified town core, after a sigil killed the chanteuse. Its basis is unclear and not discussed, so it looks like a coordinated or momentum-driven vote. My position: holding out Heat: Extremely high at the moment of voting: five players abruptly targeted me despite no open accusation in the morning discussion. Forward exposure: Claiming reveals my role and my unused bullets, which makes me a target for the wolves and the lone killer. It cannot be undone. Staying silent keeps the role hidden but leaves me facing a majority I cannot answer, and my role is revealed at death anyway. Target landscape: An unconfirmed player who had probed the dead tracker's findings, versus me. The verified investigator, sentinel and sigilist core is unthreatened. The evidence against me is behavioral and sudden, with no prior open accusations. Public vs private: I privately hold two unused vigilante bullets and no night shots taken, yet five players suddenly formed an execution bloc against me with no earlier accusation. The public read of me as suspicious contradicts my private status as a town power role.

action: In the mid/late game with 1-2 bullets and few evil factions left, spend a bullet at night instead of holding it. Rank living players by public evidence: first anyone Suspicious per a claimed investigator, caught lying, or who is the last unvetted player after mechanical clears; second a quiet player who avoided every claim and was never cleared. Shoot the top candidate. If the pool is down to you and one unvetted player, shoot that player, because passing leaves you as the obvious day vote. If both wolves are dead and a hidden lone killer remains, shoot the least-cleared quiet player rather than preserving ammo, because the remaining bullets have no later use if you are voted out. If no candidate clears a reasonable suspicion threshold (roughly 1 in 3 or better) and several confirmed town roles are alive, hold fire and keep the role hidden.
situation: Late-game night where one or two evil factions (a lone wolf or the necromancer, possibly alongside a killer) are still active. The vigilante still holds bullets and must choose between shooting a suspect and holding fire to conserve ammo and stay hidden. Holding fire in these observations left the evil faction alive, let it kill again, and left the vigilante under day suspicion or voted out with bullets unused. Information landscape: Mostly information-rich on town roles (public claims, investigator clears, healer saves), but information-starved on exactly which quiet player is the remaining killer. Wolves may already be dead. Stakes: The board is near parity, so each night's kill by the remaining evil narrows town's margin. Every unused bullet is wasted if the vigilante is voted out first. One correct shot can end or cripple the last evil faction, and one wasted night gives it another kill. Forward exposure: A shot spends a bullet irrevocably and may hit an innocent town utility role. A miss is announced and exposes the vigilante as the shooter. Holding fire stays hidden but gives up the night kill and leaves you on the daytime vote. Target landscape: A small pool of 2-4 unconfirmed living players. The claimed investigator, healer, trailseer or sentinel are publicly claimed or cleared. The candidates are quiet, unvetted players, one of whom is likely the remaining evil. Evidence comes from mechanical clears and vote records, with a thin behavioral basis for the rest.

action: When few evil players remain (one wolf left) and the board is small, spend a vigilante bullet only on a target backed by hard evidence: a check result you can trust, a caught lie, or a vote or visit pattern that ties them to the wolf. If your only candidates are claimed or cleared town members, or suspicion rests on speculation or a failed ability (such as sigils that found nothing), hold the shot and put your weight into the day vote. A wrong shot removes a town ally and a vote, and it can leave the wolves one mislynch from winning. If you decide to shoot, pick the unclaimed player who is least cleared and has the strongest tie to the surviving wolf, never a claimed or cleared role. Keep the remaining bullet unrevealed so that it stays a threat.
situation: Late game after the lone killer has been eliminated. One wolf remains among about six living players, and the vigilante considers a speculative shot at a claimed town member without any coordination with the town. Information landscape: Information-rich. The lone killer is dead, the investigator has produced system-cleared results, and several role claims are on the board. Nothing ties any specific candidate to the last wolf. Stakes: Each town death brings the wolves closer to parity. A wrong shot with six players alive and one wolf left puts the wolves one mislynch from winning, so only a shot backed by evidence is worth the risk. Forward exposure: Spending a bullet is irreversible. A morning death announcement shows the town that a vigilante is shooting. A miss kills a town player and reveals their role. The shot also tells the wolves that a vigilante is alive and where the town stands. Target landscape: Claimed town roles (sigilist, sentinel, trailseer, confirmed investigator) and an unclaiming quiet player. Suspicion of the claimed sigilist rested on failed sigils, which is behavioral and weak. Cleared players are poor targets.

action: Once you have claimed vigilante in the open, you are the wolves' obvious kill target and blocking target. Do not expect your last bullet to land on a speculative guess. Before the night, push the town toward a vote on the best-supported suspect. Fire the last bullet only at a player with concrete evidence against them, and never at one the investigator has cleared. If you have no such target, hold the shot. Leave behind a clear final statement of your reads so that your death does not create a misleading record.
situation: The vigilante has claimed publicly, the daytime vote ended in a tie, and one hidden wolf remains among about five living players. Investigations have been repeatedly roleblocked, and the vigilante guesses at the roleblocker's identity. Information landscape: Information-starved. Investigative actions were roleblocked repeatedly, so the town relies on conflicting vote reads and behavioral theories. Stakes: With five alive and one wolf, one more town death puts the wolves close to parity. A shot spent on a cleared neutral player, plus the vigilante's own death, leaves the town short of numbers. Forward exposure: Your public claim of vigilante makes you a certain target for the wolf kill and for roleblocks. A blocked shot wastes the bullet. If you die that night, your last vote and statements stay on the record and can mislead the town. Target landscape: A quiet player cleared by an investigator check, a claimed sigilist who visited no one, and a voter who sided with an eliminated wolf. The only grounds for suspicion were a speculative theory about who the roleblocker was, not evidence.

action: When you hold 2 bullets and the public record has produced hard evidence against a specific player, shoot that player at night instead of holding fire. Hard evidence means a role the Game Master revealed that disproves their claim (for example, the true healer's confirmed death exposing a rival healer claimant), or a vote deadlock around a player whose defense contradicts a Trailseer or other claim. If one candidate's story is mechanically impossible, shoot them. If several candidates are only behaviorally suspicious, hold the bullet and keep gathering information. Fire quietly, and do not reveal yourself as the vigilante before the shot.
situation: A day mis-elimination or a no-elimination tie vote left a disproven or contested claimant alive, and the vigilante holds a bullet at night. The village failed to remove the player the evidence points to, so the vigilante can remove them without a vote. Information landscape: Information-rich: a GM-confirmed role reveal, a Trailseer or other claimed visit report, and public vote records expose a contradiction in one player's story. Most other players are passive and unverified. Stakes: The board is close to wolf parity, with few players alive and wolves possibly already near equalling the rest. A single correct shot can remove a wolf, cut the pack's numbers, and strip its abilities, which may decide the game. A miss may leave Town unable to catch up. Forward exposure: The shot is announced next morning as a vigilante kill, confirming that a vigilante exists but not who it is. It irreversibly spends one of two bullets. If the target is a wolf, the pack loses a member and any remaining ability; if the target is wrong, a Town player dies and the bullet is wasted. Target landscape: Players whose claims are contradicted by a GM-announced role reveal, or who are tied or deadlocked in the day vote and whose defense conflicts with another claimant's account. Other living players are uncommitted and have no hard evidence against them. The basis is hard mechanical evidence, not behavior alone.

action: With one bullet left and three or four players alive, fire the bullet that night instead of holding it for a later day. If the board is down to a single killer and one more town death hands it parity, holding fire cannot remove that killer overnight and risks dying with the bullet unspent. Shoot the single most probable remaining killer even at roughly 50% odds, because a hit can end the game on the spot and a hold only delays a likely loss. If a shot at a Town-aligned or neutral player would not stop the killer's next kill, it still leaves you no worse off than dying unused, so commit to the best-supported read.
situation: Endgame at three or four players after the pack or one evil faction has been voted out. The vigilante has already claimed publicly and holds the last bullet. One killer remains, and a single further town death gives it parity or a win. Information landscape: Information-rich: roles revealed by deaths, vote histories, claims confirmed or contradicted by announced facts, and a short list of unaccounted-for players. Stakes: Any town death overnight ends the game, so this one shot is the last chance for Town to remove the final killer before it kills. Holding fire hands the killer the initiative and the win. Forward exposure: Irreversible and terminal. The last bullet is spent, and a hit on the killer ends the game while a miss usually leaves a wolf or killer to finish the game that night. Holding fire is no safer: the vigilante is a likely overnight kill or block target and can die with the shot unused. Target landscape: Two or three living candidates, one of whom is the remaining wolf or lone killer. Some roles are confirmed by announced reveals and wills. The rest are separated only by claims, vote records, and which players drew night actions.

action: Choose the last-bullet target by ranking the remaining candidates on hard evidence first. Prefer the player whose claim or story was contradicted by an announced role reveal or will, for example a claimed tracker or watcher whose results clash with a confirmed true sentinel. Next prefer a player whose votes pushed a confirmed Town player out or who drew early night actions. Do not default to the quiet, unclaimed player just because they are low-information, since they may be a neutral such as the speculator. Shoot the quiet player only when the claimed players are all cleared by confirmed facts.
situation: Final-bullet decision with a wolf or lone killer hidden among the last two or three other players, where the vigilante must pick by deduction rather than certainty. Information landscape: Information-rich: confirmed reveals show which claims were true and which were fabricated, leaving a narrow set of candidates separated by contradictions and voting records. Stakes: A hit wins or flips the game and a miss loses it, so the choice should follow the strongest verified contradiction rather than a hunch about who is quiet. Forward exposure: The shot is irreversible and ends the game on a hit or miss. The result is announced publicly, and a wrong shot on a neutral or Town player wastes the bullet and leaves the real killer free to strike. Target landscape: A binary or near-binary choice between a quiet unclaimed player and a claimed role-holder. The claimed player's story was contradicted by a revealed true role, while the quiet player has only behavioral suspicion.

action: With no role reveals, no check or watch results, and no vote history pointing at anyone, hold fire and keep every bullet. Treat a blind shot as mostly friendly fire against a town power role, and a shot at the Serial Killer is wasted because it is night-immune. Use the quiet night to build a firing list: voters who broke from consensus, anyone defending a revealed wolf, and any claim that is later contradicted. Shoot only once a target is backed by at least one concrete signal, such as an announced flip, a caught lie, or a claimed investigator's Suspicious result that has been corroborated. If your death looks likely next night (for example after a power role has died), fire at the best-supported name instead of dying with bullets unused.
situation: Opening night or the first nights after an abstention-heavy or no-vote day. No evil is confirmed, there are one or two deaths, and the room has only speculative reads. The vigilante has 1-2 bullets and is deciding between a blind shot and holding. Information landscape: Information-starved: no confirmed wolf or killer, no validated investigative results, and only unverified claims such as a tracker reporting zero visits or a sigil with no effect. Stakes: Evil is far from parity, so a wasted or friendly-fire bullet costs more than a one-night delay. Two evil killers are active, however, so the vigilante's bullets can be lost if it is killed unused. Moderate stakes favor holding fire until a lead exists, then converting it quickly. Forward exposure: A shot spends a non-renewable bullet and cannot be undone. If the victim dies, the morning report shows a vigilante kill, which marks the shooter as a target. A wrong shot kills town. Holding fire leaves no visit trace and keeps the role hidden, but it does not protect the vigilante from a wolf or Serial Killer kill. Target landscape: All other living players have unknown alignment and no public role claims. Voting records are empty or thin, so the only candidates are behavioral outliers such as minority voters or players pushing odd accusations. There is no mechanical evidence against any of them.

action: When a wolf has already been caught and a claimed investigator is validated, hold fire and let the investigator's checks and the daytime vote resolve the remaining suspect. This avoids a shot that could collide with night protection or kill a misread player. Hold only while the investigator and healer are alive and the town is on track to vote the suspect out. Fire at the suspect (the vocal defender of the dead wolf, or a player the investigator flags Suspicious) only if the investigator is killed or blocked and no check will land, or if your own survival is in doubt and the evidence on that suspect is convergent. If your bullets can finish the last wolf and the lone killer is gone or contained, take the shot.
situation: A wolf was just eliminated through a validated investigator claim. The investigator is exposed to night attacks, the healer is protecting, and the dead wolf's defender is the obvious remaining suspect. The vigilante decides whether to fire on that suspect or let the town's mechanics resolve it. Information landscape: Information-rich: one wolf is confirmed dead, the investigator claim is validated by the flip, and voting records isolate the surviving suspect. Stakes: One wolf is already down and the town has a working investigator and healer, so the town leads. A mistaken shot would hand tempo back to evil, so the vigilante should hold in reserve until a check or the vote fails to finish the job. Forward exposure: Holding fire keeps the vigilante hidden and both bullets in reserve, and the decision is fully reversible the next night. Shooting would reveal a vigilante and spend a bullet. It would also add a visit that can muddy Sentinel and Trailseer information while the town's own checks are working. Target landscape: The main suspect is the loud defender of a revealed wolf who voted against the validated investigator, so the case rests on voting behavior. It is corroborated or soon to be tested by a Suspicious check. The other candidates are quiet, unverified players with no evidence against them.
